# System Architecture & Fallback Flow Diagrams

This document illustrates the functional architecture, the human-in-the-loop rapid replanning workflow, and the hardened resilience fallback subsystems implemented within the application.

It reflects the in-memory state architecture (`store.js`), the Greedy Insertion replanning engine, the deterministic constraint validations, the 9-attribute local Store-and-Forward queue, and the 5-state GPS telematics degradation hierarchy.

---

## 1. High-Level System Architecture & Operational Workflow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    %% Actors
    Dispatcher([Dispatcher / Operations Manager])

    %% UI Layer
    subgraph UI ["Web UI Layer (Vanilla JS Components)"]
        Dashboard[Dashboard / Live Map]
        ReplanningView[AI Replanning & Explanation View]
        BusesView[Live Fleet Monitor & Slideout]
        PendingModal[Store-and-Forward Queue Modal]
        ManualGpsModal[Manual GPS Checkpoint Modal]
        ReportsUI[Evaluation / Reports UI]
    end

    %% State & Data Layer
    subgraph Data ["Application State & Data (store.js)"]
        MockData[(Static Mock Data)]
        AppStore[In-Memory AppStore]
        OfflineQueue[Offline LocalStorage Queue (9-Attr Schema)]
        AuditLog[(Tamper-Evident Audit Trail)]
    end

    %% Algorithmic Logic
    subgraph Engine ["Rapid Replanning Engine"]
        Trigger[Disruption Triggered]
        Evaluate[Candidate Evaluation Loop]
        
        subgraph Constraints ["Deterministic Hard Constraints"]
            CapCheck{Capacity Check}
            DrvCheck{Driver Availability & Commitments}
            CompCheck{Route Compatibility}
            AdaCheck{ADA Accessibility}
            ProgressCheck{Route Progress & Remaining Stops}
        end
        
        Rank[Weighted Heuristic Scoring & Ranking]
        Rec[Recommendation & 7-Dim Explanation Generated]
        NoFeasible[No Feasible Solution Fallback]
    end

    %% Fallback Subsystems
    subgraph Fallbacks ["Resilience & Fallback Layer"]
        NetFail[Network Disconnected]
        SyncFail[Sync Failure Handler]
        RetryEngine[Retry Mechanism & Idempotency]
        GpsDegrade[GPS Telematics Degradation Engine]
        ManGps[Manual GPS Checkpoint Override]
    end

    %% Connections - Main Workflow
    Dispatcher -->|Monitors Fleet| Dashboard
    Dashboard -->|Triggers Disruption| Trigger
    Trigger --> Evaluate
    
    Evaluate --> CapCheck
    Evaluate --> DrvCheck
    Evaluate --> CompCheck
    Evaluate --> AdaCheck
    Evaluate --> ProgressCheck
    
    CapCheck & DrvCheck & CompCheck & AdaCheck & ProgressCheck --> Rank
    Rank -->|Candidates Available| Rec
    Rank -->|All Candidates Rejected| NoFeasible
    
    Rec --> ReplanningView
    NoFeasible --> ReplanningView
    
    ReplanningView -->|Review & Accept| Dispatcher
    ReplanningView -->|Modify Constraints| Dispatcher
    ReplanningView -->|Reject Recommendation| Dispatcher
    
    Dispatcher -->|Explicit Approval| AppStore
    AppStore -->|Records Audit Event| AuditLog
    
    %% Data Connections
    MockData -->|Initial Load| AppStore
    AppStore --> UI
    AppStore --> Engine
    
    %% Fallback Connections
    NetFail -->|Enqueues Action with 9 Attributes| OfflineQueue
    OfflineQueue -->|Auto-Sync on Reconnect| AppStore
    SyncFail -->|Records Error & Increments Retry| OfflineQueue
    RetryEngine -->|Flushes Failed Items| AppStore
    
    GpsDegrade -->|LIVE / LAST_KNOWN / STALE / NO_SIGNAL| AppStore
    Dispatcher -->|Submits Radio Checkpoint| ManGps
    ManGps -->|Updates Coordinates & Source=manual| AppStore
```

---

## 2. Network Store-and-Forward Lifecycle (10 Checkpoints)

The diagram below details the operational path taken when network connectivity fluctuates during dispatcher actions:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Dispatcher as Dispatcher
    participant UI as Web UI / Header
    participant Store as AppStore (store.js)
    participant Queue as LocalStorage Queue
    participant Server as Central District Server

    Dispatcher->>UI: Trigger Operational Action (e.g., Accept Plan)
    
    alt Online State
        UI->>Store: queueAction(actionType, payload)
        Store->>Server: HTTP POST /api/dispatch (Sync)
        alt Success (200 OK)
            Server-->>Store: Synchronized Confirmation
            Store->>UI: Plan Applied & Audit Event Recorded
        else Network Drops Mid-Transmission or 5xx Error
            Server--xStore: Connection Dropped / 500 Error
            Store->>Queue: Save with status: FAILED, increment retryCount, record error
            Store->>UI: Show Banner ("1 Action Failed - Retained in Queue")
        end
    else Offline State (Network Disconnected)
        UI->>Store: queueAction(actionType, payload)
        Store->>Queue: Push Action (actionId, timestamp, userId, role, actionType, payload, status: PENDING, retryCount: 0, lastAttempt: null, error: null)
        Store->>UI: Show Toast ("Action stored locally in Store-and-Forward queue")
        Store->>UI: Update Header Banner ("OFFLINE: Pending Sync: N")
    end

    Note over Dispatcher,Server: Network Restored (online event or simulation toggle)
    Store->>UI: Banner Updates to "RESTORED: N Actions Ready to Sync"
    
    alt Automatic Sync or Dispatcher clicks "Sync All Now"
        Store->>Queue: Read FIFO Pending Items
```

# System Architecture & Workflow Diagram

This document illustrates the actual functional architecture and human-in-the-loop rapid replanning workflow implemented within the application. 

It accurately reflects the in-memory state architecture, the replanning algorithmic flow, the deterministic constraint validations, and the offline fallback capabilities currently present in the codebase.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    %% Actors
    Dispatcher([Dispatcher / Operations Manager])

    %% UI Layer
    subgraph UI ["Web UI Layer (Vanilla JS Components)"]
        Dashboard[Dashboard / Live Map]
        ReplanningView[AI Replanning View]
        ReportsUI[Evaluation / Reports UI]
    end

    %% State & Data Layer
    subgraph Data ["Application State & Data (store.js)"]
        MockData[(Static Mock Data)]
        AppStore[In-Memory AppStore]
        OfflineQueue[Offline LocalStorage Queue]
    end

    %% Algorithmic Logic
    subgraph Engine ["Rapid Replanning Engine"]
        Trigger[Disruption Triggered]
        Evaluate[Candidate Evaluation Loop]
        
        subgraph Constraints ["Deterministic Constraints"]
            CapCheck{Capacity Check}
            DrvCheck{Driver Availability & Commitments}
            CompCheck{Route Compatibility}
            ProxCheck{Proximity / Distance}
        end
        
        Rank[Scoring & Ranking]
        Rec[Recommendation Generated]
        NoFeasible[No Feasible Solution Fallback]
    end

    %% Workflow & Fallbacks
    subgraph Fallbacks ["Resilience & Fallbacks"]
        NetFail[Network Disconnected]
        GpsFail[GPS Telemetry Lost]
        ManGps[Manual GPS Override]
    end

    %% Connections - Main Workflow
    Dispatcher -->|Monitors| Dashboard
    Dashboard -->|Triggers Breakdown / Urgent Add| Trigger
    Trigger --> Evaluate
    
    Evaluate --> CapCheck
    Evaluate --> DrvCheck
    Evaluate --> CompCheck
    Evaluate --> ProxCheck
    
    CapCheck & DrvCheck & CompCheck & ProxCheck --> Rank
    Rank -->|Candidates Available| Rec
    Rank -->|All Candidates Rejected| NoFeasible
    
    Rec --> ReplanningView
    NoFeasible --> ReplanningView
    
    ReplanningView -->|Review & Accept| Dispatcher
    ReplanningView -->|Review & Modify| Dispatcher
    
    Dispatcher -->|Explicit Approval| AppStore
    
    %% Data Connections
    MockData -->|Initial Load| AppStore
    AppStore --> UI
    AppStore --> Engine
    
    %% Fallback Connections
    NetFail -->|Saves Pending Changes| OfflineQueue
    OfflineQueue -->|Syncs on Reconnect| AppStore
    
    GpsFail -->|Flags 'No Signal'| AppStore
    Dispatcher -->|Inputs Override| ManGps
    ManGps --> AppStore
```

### Architectural Notes
- **State Management:** The application relies on a single, centralized `AppStore` that handles all state transitions, notifying vanilla JS UI components of changes.
- **Human-in-the-Loop:** The AI recommendation engine evaluates permutations deterministically based on hard constraints, but the Dispatcher must explicitly review the tradeoffs and approve the `aiRecommendation` before the active `routeId` or `busId` state is modified.
- **Resilience:** The architecture natively supports network interruption (queuing changes to LocalStorage) and telemetry failure (falling back to manual checkpoint entry by the Dispatcher).

## 2. Network Store-and-Forward Fallback Architecture

### Exact Implemented Flow Pipeline

```text
Online action
      ↓
[Network Failure]
      ↓
Local Queue (localStorage)
      ↓
Pending State (status: 'PENDING')
      ↓
[Network Recovery]
      ↓
Sync Attempt (FIFO transmission)
      ↓
  ┌───────────────────┴───────────────────┐
  ↓                                       ↓
Success (status: 'SYNCED')        Sync Failure (status: 'FAILED')
                                          ↓
                                  Retry (manual / auto)
                                          ↓
                                  Success (status: 'SYNCED')
```

### Architectural Sequence Diagram

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Dispatcher as Dispatcher
    participant UI as Web UI / Header
    participant Store as AppStore (store.js)
    participant Queue as LocalStorage Queue
    participant Server as Central District Server

    Dispatcher->>UI: Trigger Operational Action (e.g., Accept Plan)
    
    alt Online State
        UI->>Store: queueAction(actionType, payload)
        Store->>Server: HTTP POST /api/dispatch (Sync)
        alt Success (200 OK)
            Server-->>Store: Synchronized Confirmation
            Store->>UI: Plan Applied & Audit Event Recorded
        else Network Drops Mid-Transmission or 5xx Error
            Server--xStore: Connection Dropped / 500 Error
            Store->>Queue: Save with status: FAILED, increment retryCount, record error
            Store->>UI: Show Banner ("1 Action Failed - Retained in Queue")
        end
    else Offline State (Network Disconnected)
        UI->>Store: queueAction(actionType, payload)
        Store->>Queue: Push Action (actionId, timestamp, userId, role, actionType, payload, status: PENDING, retryCount: 0, lastAttempt: null, error: null)
        Store->>UI: Show Toast ("Action stored locally in Store-and-Forward queue")
        Store->>UI: Update Header Banner ("OFFLINE: Pending Sync: N")
    end

    Note over Dispatcher,Server: Network Restored (online event or simulation toggle)
    Store->>UI: Banner Updates to "RESTORED: N Actions Ready to Sync"
    
    alt Automatic Sync or Dispatcher clicks "Sync All Now"
        Store->>Queue: Read FIFO Pending Items
        loop For Each Pending Action
            Store->>Store: Deduplication Check (Idempotent actionId)
            Store->>Server: Sync Action Request
            alt Server Accepts
                Server-->>Store: 200 OK
                Store->>Queue: Mark SYNCED and remove from queue
            else Sync Fails
                Server--xStore: Connection Interrupted / Server Busy
                Store->>Queue: Set status: FAILED, retryCount++, record error
                Note over Store,Queue: Action is NEVER lost and NEVER falsely shown synced
            end
        end
        Store->>UI: Refresh Pending Queue Count & Modal
    end

    alt Dispatcher clicks "Retry Failed Actions"
        Dispatcher->>UI: Click "Retry Failed Actions"
        UI->>Store: retryFailedActions()
        Store->>Queue: Reset FAILED items to PENDING
        Store->>Server: Re-attempt Synchronization
    end
```

### Component Details

- **Pending Actions:**
  - Persisted in browser `localStorage` under `schoolbus_offline_queue`.
  - Every action adheres to the mandatory 9-attribute schema:
    1. `actionId` (String): Unique transaction ID (e.g. `ACT-1727618293-A4F9`).
    2. `timestamp` (String): ISO-8601 creation time.
    3. `userId` (String): Dispatcher ID (e.g. `DISPATCHER-01`).
    4. `role` (String): Authority level (`Dispatcher`, `Admin`).
    5. `actionType` (String): Operation name (`REPLAN_ACCEPT`, `REPLAN_MODIFY`, `CANCELLATION_APPROVE`, `MANUAL_OVERRIDE`).
    6. `payload` (Object): Immutable operational parameters, route version keys, and target entities.
    7. `status` (String): Lifecycle state (`PENDING`, `SYNCING`, `SYNCED`, `FAILED`).
    8. `retryCount` (Number): Integer count of sync attempts (begins at `0`).
    9. `lastAttempt` (String / Null): Timestamp of the most recent sync attempt.
    10. `error` (String / Null): Server or connection failure diagnostic message.
  - Pending actions maintain strict FIFO ordering and full visibility via header badge counters and the interactive Queue Management Modal.

- **Duplicate Prevention:**
  - The queue intercepts duplicate action dispatches via unique `actionId` matching.
  - If an action with an identical `actionId` is already queued or processed, re-submission is suppressed without appending duplicate entries, modifying route version keys, or double-allocating passengers.

- **Sync Failure:**
  - When a transmission error occurs during background sync, the system explicitly marks the action as `FAILED`.
  - The item is **never discarded** and is **never marked as synced**.
  - `retryCount` increments by 1, and the specific failure reason is captured in the `error` property for diagnostic inspection.

- **Retry Behavior:**
  - When connectivity is restored, the queue triggers automatic FIFO synchronization.
  - Dispatchers can manually trigger retries via **Retry Failed Actions** in the top alert banner or Queue Modal.
  - Retrying sets all `FAILED` items back to `PENDING` and re-initiates the sync attempt.

## 3. GPS Telematics Degradation & Fallback Architecture

### Exact Implemented Degradation Pipeline

```text
LIVE GPS (Fresh fix: age <= 60s)
      ↓
[Signal drop / telemetry pause: age 60s - 120s]
      ↓
LAST_KNOWN GPS (Retains last verified fix, age visible, reduced trust)
      ↓
[Telemetry elapsed: age > 120s]
      ↓
STALE GPS (Warning banner, low trust, distance penalties, dispatcher verification)
      ↓
[Signal completely lost / dead zone]
      ↓
NO_SIGNAL (Dead zone indicator, last-known location only, zero trust)
      ↓
[Dispatcher VHF radio / landmark report]
      ↓
MANUAL Fallback (Source identified as MANUAL / manual_dispatcher, verified trust)
```

### State Machine Transition Diagram

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> LIVE: GPS Ping (< 60s ago)
    
    LIVE --> LAST_KNOWN: Signal Interrupt (60s - 120s old)
    note right of LIVE
        Trust: HIGH (1.0)
        Badge: 🛰️ Live Fix (Green)
        Automated Distance Ranking
        Freshness: age <= 60s
    end note

    LAST_KNOWN --> STALE: Age > 120 seconds
    note right of LAST_KNOWN
        Trust: REDUCED (0.7)
        Badge: ⏱️ Last Known (Amber)
        Displays exact age in seconds
        Never shown as Live
    end note

    STALE --> NO_SIGNAL: Telemetry Lost / Dead Zone
    note right of STALE
        Trust: LOW (0.4)
        Badge: ⚠️ Stale Fix (Orange)
        Amber Warning Banner displayed
        Penalizes distance-based score
        Requires Dispatcher Verification
    end note

    NO_SIGNAL --> MANUAL: Dispatcher Radio Checkpoint
    note right of NO_SIGNAL
        Trust: MINIMAL (0.1)
        Badge: 📡 No Signal (Red)
        Dead-reckoning / last stop only
        Explicit "Not Live" warning
        Manual Location input prompted
    end note

    MANUAL --> LIVE: Vehicle GPS Re-acquired (< 60s)
    note right of MANUAL
        Trust: VERIFIED (0.9)
        Badge: 📍 Manual Checkpoint (Blue)
        Dispatcher-confirmed fix
        Stores lat, lng, landmark, source='manual_dispatcher'
    end note
```

### Telemetry Details & Integrity Rules

- **GPS Age Calculation:**
  - `ageSeconds` is computed dynamically as `Math.max(0, Math.floor((Date.now() - new Date(bus.lastUpdated).getTime()) / 1000))`.
  - Consistently stored and rendered alongside all 5 core telemetry fields: `latitude`, `longitude`, `source`, `lastUpdated`, and `ageSeconds`.
  - Displayed prominently in seconds/minutes across vehicle monitors, slideout panels, map tooltips, and recommendation uncertainty cards.

- **Stale GPS Warning:**
  - When telemetry age exceeds 120 seconds or is flagged stale, the system displays an amber warning banner:
    `WARNING: "GPS data is X minutes old. Distance-based ranking may be inaccurate."`
  - The vehicle badge switches to `⚠️ Stale Fix (Not Live)`.
  - Trust level is lowered to `LOW (0.4)`, reducing algorithmic confidence in distance calculations during candidate evaluation.

- **Manual Location Fallback:**
  - If a bus's GPS is in `NO_SIGNAL`, `STALE`, or disabled, dispatchers can enter a verified checkpoint location via the **Manual GPS Fix** modal or vehicle slideout.
  - Dispatchers can enter latitude/longitude coordinates or select predefined landmarks (e.g. *Central Depot*, *Cole & Haight St Checkpoint*).
  - The system updates the bus state, sets `source: 'manual_dispatcher'`, `sourceUpper: 'MANUAL'`, `isManual: true`, `isLive: false`, resets `ageSeconds: 0`, and records a `MANUAL_OVERRIDE` audit event.

- **Dispatcher Verification Requirement:**
  - Whenever replanning involves a bus or driver with degraded telemetry (`STALE`, `LAST_KNOWN`, or `NO_SIGNAL`), the engine flags the candidate with `requiresDispatcherConfirmation: true` and `requiresDispatcherVerification: true`.
  - The recommendation explanation explicitly displays a verification badge, preventing automated unconfirmed dispatch and requiring the dispatcher to inspect the telemetry warning before approval.
